Customized courses for Agniveers  
 
1946. Shri Niranjan Bishi: 
Dr. Prashanta Nanda: 
 
Will the Minister of Education be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government is planning to launch customized courses for the 
Agniveers to enable them pursue higher education/profession once their contract 
under Agnipath is over; 
 
(b) how such a programme will differ from equivalent conventional courses; 
 
(c) how does Government plan to compensate for the lost four years of education while 
the Agniveers are in service; and 
 
(d) whether Government will provide any assistance/preference to the Agniveers in  
providing employment or places in higher education institutions post the contract? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SMT. ANNPURNA DEVI) 
 
(a) to (d):  Yes Sir , Indira Gandhi National Open University (IGNOU) has designed 
customized courses which recognizes in-service training as credits for Graduation degree for 
the eligible Defence Forces personnel including Agniveers. 
 
IGNOU has prepared a specially designed 120-credit B achelor’s degree programme 
for the serving Defence Forces personnel including Agniveers, with a provision of giving up 
to 50% credit to the skill education/training (both technical and non-technical) imparted to 
them during service. The regulatory bodies – University Grants Commission (UGC),  All 
India Council for Technical Education (AICTE),  National Council of Vocational Education 
and Training (NCVET) have given in principle approval. 
 
A Bachelor’s degree will be awarded on successful completion of the programme 
requirements as per prescribed norms. The degree will be equivalent to any other similar 
conventional course duly recognized by AICTE and UGC.

Planning to construct ‘PM Shri Schools’ 
 
1947.         SHRI VIVEK  K. TANKHA:  
 
Will the
 Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details of ‘PM Shri Schools’;  
 
(b)  whether Government is planning to construct 15,000 PM Shri schools, as announced, 
in addition to the Kendriya Vidyalayas (KVs), if so, State-wise details thereof; 
 
(c)  if not, the reasons therefor; and  
 
(d)  what is the Central Government future expansion policy in respect of Kendriya 
Vidyalayas, the details thereof? 
 
 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION  
(SMT. ANNPURNA DEVI) 
 
(a) to (c):  The Finance Minister in her Budget Speech on 01.02.2021 has announced to 
qualitatively strengthen more than 15,000 schools from across the country to include all 
components of the National Education Policy, 2020. The objective is to develop them as 
exemplar schools in their regions, handholding and mentoring other schools to achieve the 
ideals of the policy. 
(d) Opening of new Kendriya Vidyalayas (KVs) is a continuous process. KVs are 
opened primarily to cater to the educational needs of the wards of transferable Central 
Government Employees including Defence & Para-military personnel, Central Autonomous 
Bodies, Central Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) and Central Institute of Higher Learning 
(IHL) by providing a common programme of education throughout the country. Proposals 
for opening of new KVs are considered only if sponsored by Ministries or Departments of 
the Government of India/State Governments/Union Territories Administrations and 
committing resources for setting up a new KV. 
      The proposals received from various sponsoring authorities found fulfilling the 
mandatory pre-requisites for opening of new KVs have to compete with other such 
proposals under the “challenge Method” and is subject to approval of the competent 
authority.

Duties of school teachers in NCT Delhi 
 
1949.   DR. C.M. RAMESH:  
        
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
a) the details of school teachers in NCT Delhi who have been put on different duties other 
than academics  during the last three years, duty-wise and school-wise; and  
b)  whether any gender bar and age bar have been prescribed before school teachers of NCT 
Delhi are inducted in such duties, the details thereof? 
 
 
A N S W E R 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SMT. ANNPURNA DEVI) 
 
(a) & (b)   Education is in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and majority of the 
schools are under the administrative control of respe  ctive States and Union Territories (UT). 
Further, the recruitment, service conditions and deployment of teachers are primarily  in the 
domain of the respective State Government/UT Administration. 
  
The section 27 of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 
states that “no teacher shall be deployed for any non -educational purposes other than the 
decennial population census, disaster relief duties or duties relating to elections to the local 
authority or the State Legislatures or Parliament, as the case may be”. The Ministry of 
Education has also issued guidelines to all States and UTs that emphasize tha t teachers should 
not be deployed for non -educational duties other than those which are in accordance with the 
RTE Act.

Girl enrolment in secondary schools in various States under SSA 
 
1950 Shri Sanjay Raut: 
 
      Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) has been able to achieve the objective for which it was set up 
and if so, the details thereof and if not, the corrective steps taken in this regard; 
 
(b)  the number of elementary, secondary and higher secondary schools that have been upgraded under SSA 
during each of the last three years and current year in the State of Maharashtra; and 
 
(c)  the current school enrolment rate of girls at secondary level along-with States that have been continuously 
lagging behind in increasing the percentage of girls enrolment in secondary schools? 
 
A N S W E R 
 
 MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SMT. ANNPURNA DEVI) 
 
(a) & (b): The Department of School Education and Literacy with effect from 2018-19 has launched an 
Integrated Centrally Sponsored Scheme for School Education- Samagra Shiksha. The scheme has now been 
aligned with the recommendations of NEP 2020 to ensure that all children have access to quality education with 
an equitable and inclusive classroom environment which should take care of their diverse background, 
multilingual needs, different academic abilities and make them active participants in the learning  process. 
 
  The major objectives of the Scheme are: (i) Support States and UTs in implementing the 
recommendations of the National Education Policy 2020; (ii) Support States in implementation of Right of 
Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009; (iii) Focus on Early Childhood Care and Education; (iv) 
Emphasis on Foundational Literacy and Numeracy; (v) Thrust on Holistic, Integrated, Inclusive and activity 
based Curriculum and Pedagogy to impart 21st century skills among the students; (vi) Provision of quality 
education and enhancing learning outcomes of students; (vii) Bridging Social and Gender Gaps in School 
Education; (viii) Ensuring equity and inclusion at all levels of school education; (ix) Strengthening and up-
gradation of State Councils for Educational Research and Training /State Institutes of Education and District 
Institutes for Education and Training as nodal agency for teacher training; (x) Ensuring safe, secure and 
conducive learning environment and maintenance of standards in schooling provisions and (xi) Promoting 
vocational education. No elementary, secondary and higher secondary school is up-graded under Samagra 
Shiksha in the State of Maharashtra.  
 
(c):  As per the Unified District Information System for Education (UDISE+) 2021, the state-wise current 
school enrollment rate of girls at Secondary level is at Annexure.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1952 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 03.08.2022 
 
Literacy status in Telangana 
1952 Dr. K. Laxman: 
Will the Minister of Education be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of support provided by Central Government to the State Government of Telangana 
under the Samagra Shiksha scheme in the last three years; 
(b) whether fund provided by Central Government was completely utilized by the State 
Government in the last three years, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether there is a huge gender divide of literacy rate in Telangana among five States in the 
country with lowest literacy rate; 
(d) if so, any action plan shared by the State Government to curb the gender literacy divide in 
Telangana, the details thereof; and 
(e) district-wise data for enrolment of girls in schools in Telangana? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRIMATI ANNPURNA DEVI) 
 
(a) & (b): The Department of School Education and Literacy has launched the Samagra Shiksha 
- an Integrated Scheme for School Education, throughout the country as a Centrally Sponsored 
Scheme with effect from Financial Year 2018-19. It is an overarching programme for the school 
education sector extending from pre-school to class XII and aims to ensure inclusive and 
equitable quality education at all levels of school education. It envisages the ‘school’ as a 
continuum from pre-school, primary, upper primary, secondary to senior secondary levels. The 
States/UTs are assisted by the Central Government to implement the Samagra Shiksha as a 
programme for providing universal access and retention, bridging the gender and social category 
gaps in education and enhancement of learning level of children at all levels of school education. 
The details of support provided by Central Government to the State Government of Telangana 
under the Samagra Shiksha scheme and 
its utilization in the last three years are as under: 
 
169

 
 
(Rs. in lakhs) 
 
Financial Year Central Releases 
Expenditure  
(including State Share) 
2019-20 109524.00 158520.45 
2020-21 34807.36 105952.79 
2021-22 55327.91 95397.23 
(Source: PRABANDH) 
 
(c): Government of India has approved a new Centrally Sponsored Scheme, namely, “New  India 
Literacy Programme (NILP)” with the aim to support the States and Union Territories in  
promoting literacy among non-literates in the age group of 15 and above, across the country 
covering 5 crore non-literates during the implementation period from 2022-27. The scheme has 
been approved with a financial outlay of Rs.1037.90 crore including Central share of Rs.700.00 
crore and State share of Rs.337.90 crore. 
 
The literacy data in the country is collected through decennial census operation conducted by 
Registrar General of India. The last Census was held in 2011. As per the Census 2011, the adult 
literacy rate (in the age group 15 and above) in the country was 69.28 percent (Adult Male 
literacy rate was 78.84 per cent and female literacy rate was 59.26 per cent). The State of 
Telangana was created on 2 nd June,
 2014 and since then no fresh Census data has officially been 
released by the Registrar General of India. As such the official data of literacy rate in Telangana 
is not available.  
 
(d): To address the gender gap in school education,
 Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas 
(KGBVs) have been sanctioned in Educationally Backward Blocks (EBBs) in Telangana . 
KGBVs are residential schools from class VI to XII for girls belonging to disadvantaged groups 
such as SC, ST, OBC, Minority and Below Poverty Line (BPL). 
 
Provision has been made to upgrade the existing KGBVs at upper primary level to senior 
secondary level. The scheme aims to provide access and quality education to girls  from  
disadvantaged  groups  by  setting  up   residential  schools  from  upper primary  to senior 
secondary level and to ensure smooth transition of girls from elementary to secondary and up to 
class XII wherever possible. 
170

 
Total 738 KGBVs have been sanctioned (20 under Type I, 280 under Type II, 195 under Type III 
and 243 under Type IV). Out of 738 KGBVs, 696 KGBVs are functional with 124701 girls ’ 
enrolment against 136500 targeted girls’ enrolment.

OBC (47.96%), 1400 are Muslims (1.12%) and 1990 are BPL category (1.60%). 
 
(e): The district-wise data for enrolment of girls in schools in Telangana is enclosed as 
Annexure.

UNSTARRED QUESTION No-1953 
TO BE ANSWERED ON- 03/08/2022 
 
EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTION IN MAHARASHTRA 
 
1953. SHRI ANIL DESAI: 
 
Will the Minister of Education be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether there is sufficient higher education al institutions in Maharashtra in proportion to 
population of the State;  
 
(b) whether Government grants permission and provides assistance to students for pursuing 
higher education abroad; 
 
(c) whether the same education is available in all the States and Government encourage or pursue 
the students to take it within the State or country; and 
 
(d) if so, the details thereof?  
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUBHAS SARKAR) 
 
(a) As per the All India Survey on Higher Education (AISHE) 2019-20, there are 53
 Higher 
Education Institutions (HEIs) per lakh  of the young population (age group 18 to 23 years) in 
Maharashtra, while the national average is 39 HEIs per lakh population. 
 
(b) Different Ministries of the Government , such as Ministries of Social Justice & 
Empowerment, Tribal Affairs, Science & Technology  and Minority Affairs,  provide financial 
assistance and interest subsidy to eligible students for pursuing higher education abroad . As far 
as Ministry of Education is concerned, no permission is required or granted as such for pursuing 
higher education abroad. 
(c) & (d) Education is in the Concurrent List, with HEIs falling under Central Government, State 
Governments, regulatory bodies, etc. The Ministry is committed to providing quality higher 
education in 
the country and encouraging students to study in India, with own initiatives and also 
augmenting the efforts of the State Governments. In this regard, the University Grants 
Commission ( UG
C) has introduced “Institution of Eminence” to support selected existing 
Government and private institutions to achieve world class status and published guidelines for 
“Internationalization of Higher Education”. 
Various other schemes, namely, Rashtriya Uchchatar 
Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA), Global Initiative for Academic Network (GIAN), Technical 
Education Quality Improvement Programme (TEQIP), Study Webs of Active-Learning for 
Young Aspiring Minds (SWAYAM), National Digital Library (NDL), Campus Connect 
Programme, Unnat Bharat Abhiyan, National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) are also 
being implemented to improve the quality of Higher education. Further, All India Council of 
Technical Education (AICTE) has revamped the existing curriculum and launched outcome 
based model curriculum for Diploma, Undergraduate and Post Graduate Courses in Engineering 
and PGDM/MBA Courses.
 
 
173

As a result of the se efforts, more Indian HEIs are debuting in the world rank lists on various 
parameters conducted by the ranking bodies. As per the QS World University Rankings 2023, 27 
Indian HEIs made it into the global top 1000.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1954 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 3RD AUGUST, 2022 
Ed-tech companies and data protection 
1954 Shri Binoy Viswam: 
Shri Abdul Wahab: 
Will the Minister of Education be pleased to state: 
(a) the list of all ed-tech companies that are currently receiving public funds from the Ministry or 
any other Ministry through any financial MoU, details of these engagements; 
(b) whether Government has developed/implemented data protection rules to safeguard the 
children in schools across the country, if so, details thereof; 
(c) steps undertaken by Government to ensure compliance with the data protection regulations by 
companies producing proprietary software; 
(d) whether there is any provision by which a parent can demand removal of all information 
collected on their child by ed-tech companies; and 
(e) total number of ed-tech companies currently operating in the country? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SMT ANNPURNA DEVI) 
(a) to (e)    
The Ministry is not providing any fund to EDTECH companies. In order to safeguard 
against the exploitative practices of ed-tech companies, the Government has issued advisory which 
includes do’s and don’ts for the stakeholders. It has also reiterated legal provisions for e -commerce 
firms (which were notified by the MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC 
DISTRIBUTION (Department of Consumer Affairs)) for information to citizens who are 
consumers of ed-tech services. The details may be seen at: 
https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1784582
 
Further, considering grievances against Ed-tech platforms, UGC and AICTE have issued 
public notices on 16th January, 2022 advising the students to check recognition/entitlement status of 
programme on official website before enrolling any course. The notice may be seen at 
https://deb.ugc.ac.in/pdf/UGC_Public_Notice_16-01
-2022.pdf. 
Section 43A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 and the Information Technology 
(Reasonable security practices and procedures and sensitive personal data or information) Rules, 
175

2011 provide safeguards for sensitive personal data or information collected. This act also provides 
for compensation to be paid to the affected users by the body corporate for failure to protect 
sensitive personal information causing wrongful gain or wrongful loss to any person. 
Also, the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) 
Rules, 2021 notified under the Information Technology Act, 2000 requires that the intermediary 
shall publish the rules and regulations, privacy policy, and user agreement for access or usage of its 
computer resource by any person.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.1955 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 03.08.2022 
 
Changes made in NCERT books 
1955 Shri Pramod Tiwari: 
Shri John Brittas : 
Will the Minister of Education be pleased to state: 
(a) the details regarding changes made in Central and State Board school books during the 
last five years; 
(b) whether it is a fact that information regarding Gujarat riots, Mughal rule in the country, 
Naxalite movement and certain Dalit writers, among other things, have been removed from 
NCERT books under a ‘rationalisation’ process; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; 
(d) if so, what was the criteria used to determine the information to be removed from the 
books; and 
(e) the steps taken to improve school education during the last five years? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SMT.ANNPURNA DEVI) 
 
(a): The National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT), as a regular 
activity, update their textbooks before these are reprinted every year by incorporating new 
priorities and initiatives occurred at the National level.   In 2017-18, NCERT undertook this 
exercise and updated data in view of the then latest available databases such as census survey, 
etc.  In 2018-19, NCERT, on the basis of suggestions received from various stakeholders, 
rationalized content of the textbooks in all the subject areas across the classes. In 2020-21, 
changes with regard to data, etc., were included as regular exercise. In 2021-22 , to deal with 
the academic situation arising from the pandemic, major exercise of rationalization of content 
of textbooks was 
undertaken.  
 
177

(b) and (c): During the COVID-19 pandemic situation, students across the stages of school 
education have struggled a lot to continue their learning through online and other modes. 
Also, concerns related to curriculum load including the content load spread over syllabi and 
textbooks have been raised from different corners. Further, National Education Policy (NEP) 
2020 states that ‘the reduction in content and increased flexibility of school curriculum and 
the renewed emphasis on constructive rather than rote learning must be accompanied by 
parallel changes in school textbooks ’.
 With a view to facilitate speedy recovery in students 
learning continuum and compensating time loss, NCERT took a step towards the 
rationalisation of textbooks across the stages and subject areas,
 keeping a balanced approach. 
The details are available at https://ncert.nic.in/rationalised-content.php  
 
(d) NCERT has informed that the following criteria were developed for the rationalisation of 
content load:  
a.  Overlapping with similar content included in other subject area in the same class; 
b.  Similar content included in the lower or higher class in same subject; 
c.  Difficulty level; 
d.  Content, which is easily accessible to children and does not require much intervention 
from the teachers and can be learned through self-learning or peer learning; 
e.  Content, which is not relevant in the present context or outdated; 
f.  Taking care of the Learning Outcomes already developed across the classes. 
 
(e)  Some of major steps taken to improve the school education in last five years are as under: 
a. Development of Learning Outcomes for across the classes from class 1-12.  
b. Design and Development of an integrated programme of capacity building for 
teachers, teacher educat ors and education functionaries entitled ‘National 
Initiative for Sc hool Heads’ and Teachers’ Holistic Advancement’ –
 
NISHTHA.  Till now NISHTHA for elementary, secondary, Foundational 
Literacy and Numeracy and also for ECCE has been launched.  
c. National Achievement Survey in 2017 and 2021 to check the health of 
education system and provide necessary interventions to fill-up the gaps.  
d.
 Bridge Course for the elementary stage.  
e. Variety teaching-learning resources and e-content across the stages for 
supporting students, teachers and teacher educators. 
f. Experiential and joyful learning. 
178

g. Alternative Academic Calendar during Covid-19. 
h. Emphasis on Foundational Literacy and Numeracy through National Initiative 
for Proficiency in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy - NIPUN 
Bharat.  
i. Introduction of Structured Assessment for Analysing Learning (SAFAL), a 
Competency Based Education and Assessment for Grades 3,5 and 8 to assess 
core concepts, application of knowledge, and higher order thinking skills. 
j. Introduction of 360, multidimensional Holistic Progress Card that reflects in 
great detail the progress as well as the uniqueness of each learner in the 
cognitive, affective and psychomotor domains.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1956 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 03.08.2022 
 
Exemption from CUET 
1956 Shri John Brittas: 
 
Will the Minister of Education be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Government has exempted any Central University from the ambit of Common 
University Entrance Test (CUET); 
(b) if so, the details thereof and reasons therefor; 
(c) whether there is any established rules for such exemption; 
(d) whether Government will agree to new demands by the States to exempt Central 
Universities in those States which are having same or similar characteristics of Central 
Universities already exempted; 
(e) whether Government has any plans to expand the purview of CUET to cover admissions to 
the State and private Universities; and 
(f) if so, 
the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUBHAS SARKAR) 
 
(a) to (f): In pursuance of the National Education Policy, 2020, it was decided to conduct  
common entrance test for admission in Central Universities under Ministry of Education from 
the academic year 2022-23 to reduce the burden on students, universities and the entire 
education system. No Central Universities have been exempted from the ambit of Common 
University Entrance Test (CUET
). However, given the operational difficulties in some of the 
Central Universities in the North Eastern Region namely Sikkim University, Rajiv Gandhi 
University, Manipur University, Assam University, Tezpur University, Nagaland University, 
Tripura University, Mizoram University, North Eastern Hill University (NEHU) as well as 
Hemvati Nandan Bahuguna Garhwal University (HNBGU) have been allowed to take 
admission in their affiliated colleges as per the past practice for the year 2022-23 only. CUET 
is optional for State and Private Universities.

University Grants Commission 
 
1959 Shri Kamakhya Prasad Tasa: 
 
Will the Minister of Education be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether it is a fact that the University Grants Commission (UGC) is charged with 
coordination, determination and maintenance of standards of higher education and it 
provides recognition to Universities in the country and disbursements of funds to such 
recognized universities and colleges; 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c) the total numbers of institutions banned by UGC; and 
 
(d) the total institutions that get benefits given by UGC? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(Dr. SUBHAS SARKAR) 
 
(a) & (b): Under the provisions of section 12 of The University Grants Commission (UGC) ,  
Act, 1956 it has been stated that it shall be the general duty of the Commission to take, in 
consultation with the Universities or other bodies concerned, all such steps as it may think fit 
for the promotion and co -ordination of University education and for the determination and 
maintenance of standards of teaching, examination and research in Universities.  Allocation 
and disbursement of Grants to  Universities has been specified as one of the functions of the 
Commission in The UGC Act, 1956.   
  
(c): The UGC has informed that 14 Institutions have been  banned by the UGC for 
disbursement of Grants. 
 
(d): The UGC has further informed that  394 Universities/Deemed to be Universities and 
10360 colleges are in the UGC list under s ection 12 B of the UGC Act, 1956 , which makes 
them eligible for receiving grants from the Central Government, the Commission, or any 
other organisation receiving any funds from the Central Government. The major beneficiaries 
of the grants  directly disbursed by UGC are the Centrally funded HEIs which include 45 
Central Universities,  08 Inter Uni versity Centres , 22 Educational Multimedia Research 
Centres, 04 National Facilities Centres, 66 Human Resource Development Centres, 53 
Colleges of Delhi University , 04 C olleges of Banaras Hindu University , Panjab University 
Chandigarh, 08 identified Deemed  to be Universities  and 14 schemes of 
Scholarships/Fellowships. UGC also provides occasional grants to various Higher 
Educational Institutions under different schemes of UGC.

(c):   The NSIGSE scheme was evaluated in the year 2020-21 by Institute of Economic Growth

 Allocation for Children with Special Needs (CwSN) increased from Rs. 3000 per child 
per annum to Rs. 3500 per child per annum. Stipend of Rs. 200 per month for Girls with 
Special Needs from Classes 1 to 12.

Health Centres etc. Patients requiring more advanced / emergency 
treatment are evacuated through helicopter (especially deployed for 
medical evacuation purpose) to specialized medical institutions in the

ainland.

CASTE BASED RECRUITMENT IN CPMFS 
 
1964.      SHRI V. VIJAYASAI REDDY: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether it is a fact that armed forces do not recruit on the basis of 
caste of candidates; 
 
(b) whether it is also a fact that recruitment in Central Para Military Force 
(CPMFs) is done on the basis of castes and reservation; 
 
(c) whether it is also a fact that if there is a SC vacancy in any CPMF, it 
has to be filled only with the SC candidate otherwise it will upset the 
entire quota system; and 
 
(d) if so, the corrective step taken by the Ministry? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
 
(a)    The selection process in Armed Forces is open to all citizens 
without any discrimination on the basis of caste. 
 
(b)     The recruitment in Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) & Assam 
Rifles is not made on the basis of caste.  However, reservation is provided 
for SC, ST, OBC and Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) category in 
accordance with the extant policy of the Government. 
 
(c) & (d) Vacancies reserved for SC category are filled up from the 
candidates belonging to SC category only. As per the reservation policy of 
the Government, unfilled vacancies of SC quota are carried forward to 
subsequent recruitment cycle.

NATIONAL DISASTER RISK MANAGEMENT FUND 
 
1965.      SHRI V. VIJAYASAI REDDY: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether it is a fact that 15th Finance Commission has recommended 
for creation of National Disaster Risk Management Fund (NDRMF) for 
award period to mitigate measures to control sea-level rise; 
 
(b) if so, steps taken by Government to create NDRMF at the Centre and 
State levels; 
 
(c) the steps Government has taken to prevent sea erosion and 
resettlement of displaced families affected by sea erosion, with particular 
reference to Andhra Pradesh since it has the second-longest coast in the 
country and has nearly 29 per cent erosion; and 
 
(d) the vulnerability of the coast of Andhra Pradesh as per Indian National 
Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS)? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
 
(a) to (c): The 15 th Finance Commission has recommended for creation of 
National Disaster Risk Management Fund (NDRMF) at the national level. 
The total allocation for NDRMF is Rs. 68,463 Crore for the period from 
2021-22  to 2025-26.   It  is  divided 
 as  National  Disaster  Response  Fund 
 
 
193

 
-2- 
R.S.US.Q.NO. 1965 FOR 03.08.2022 
 
 (NDRF) and National Disaster Mitigation Fund (NDMF) in 80:20 ratio .  
Further, under NDMF, there is an earmarked allocation of Rs. 1,500 Crore 
for mitigation measures to prevent erosion for the award period.  In 
addition, under the Recovery and Reconstruction funding window of NDRF, 
there is an earmarked allocation of Rs. 1,000 Crore for resettlement of 
displaced people affected by erosion.  
 
Union Government has constituted NDMF on 05.02.2021.  Union 
Government has also advised all the State Governments to set up State 
Disaster Mitigation Fund (SDMFs).  So far, 21 States have intimated setting 
up of SDMF.   
 
Ministry of Earth Sciences through its institutes is providing technical 
solutions and advice to the State Governments to deal with coastal 
erosion threats. 
 
(d) As per Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services 
(INCOIS), majority of the coastal stretches of Andhra Pradesh are 
classified as Low and Medium Vulnerable classes, with 43.35% and 33.27% 
of the total coastline, respectively.  20.84% are under high vulnerability 
and 0.55% of the coastlines are classified under very high vulnerability.

TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 3RD AUGUST, 2022/ SRAVANA 12, 1944 (SAKA) 
 
ILLEGAL MIGRATION THROUGH BORDER 
 
1966 #      SMT. GEETA ALIAS CHANDRAPRABHA: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether it is a fact that there has been a decline in the number of 
people illegally migrating to India from across the border in the last two 
years; 
 
(b) if so, the decline in terms of percentage reported in illegal migration; 
 
(c) whether there is a problem of illegal migration even at the Nepal border 
in Uttar Pradesh; and 
 
(d) if so, whether Government has taken any step to resolve this matter, if 
so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
 
(a) to (d): Illegal migrants try to sneak into India in a clandestine and 
surreptitious manner mainly through difficult mountainous and reverine 
terrains along the international borders. Therefore it is not feasible to 
maintain their accurate data. Central Government has adopted a multi- 
pronged approach to ensure effective surveillance and domination of land 
borders to check infiltration of illegal migrants. Physical infrastructure in 
the  form  of border fencing, floodlighting, construction of border roads and  
 
195

-2- 
R.S.US.Q.NO. 1966 FOR 03.08.2022 
 
establishment of border outposts has been created. Vulnerable border 
outposts are regularly reviewed and strengthened by deploying additional 
manpower, special surveillance equipments and other force multipliers.  A 
technological solution in the form of Comprehensive Integrated Border 
Management System (CIBMS) has been implemented in some vulnerable 
border areas.  Border guarding forces conduct regular patrolling, lay nakas 
and establish observation posts and carry out anti- tunneling exercises to 
stop illegal infiltration.  Central Government has issued advisory to Border 
Security Force and Assam Rifles to maintain strict vigilance and 
surveillance and to take all possible steps for preventing illegal infiltration 
at International Borders.

-2- 
R.S.US.Q.NO. 1968 FOR 03.08.2022 
(b) & (c):   In January, 2016,  it was decided to reserve 33% posts at 
Constable level for being filled up by women in CRPF & CISF to begin with 
and 14-15% posts at Constable level in border guarding forces i.e. BSF,  
SSB & ITBP. The Steps taken to encourage recruitment of women 
personnel in CAPFs & AR are at Annexure. 
 
***** 
  
201

ANNEXURE 
R.S.U.S.Q.No.1968  for 03.08.2022 
 
Steps taken to encourage the recruitment of Women candidates in CAPFs & ARs 
1. Recruitment is being conducted by making wide publicity through print/electronic 
media. All female candidates are exempted from payment of application fee. 
2. There are relaxations in Physical Standard Test (PST) and Physical Efficiency 
Test(PET) for all female candidates for recruitment in CAPFs  in comparison to Male 
candidates.   
3. Facilities already available under the Central Government like Maternity Leave, Child 
Care Leave, are also applicable to CAPFs women personnel. 
4. One female member is detailed as member of the board for making recruitment of 
women personnel. 
5. Creches and Day Care Centres have been provided by the CAPFs to women 
employees. 
6. Committees have been constituted at all levels to check sexual harassment and to 
expeditiously deal with the complaints of women personnel. 
7. Women personnel are given equal opportunity in their career progression i.e. 
promotion/seniority as per the RRs at par with male counter parts. 
8. A women candidate pregnant of 12 weeks standing or over is declared temporarily 
unfit and her appointment is held in abeyance until the confinement is over. She is re-
examined for Physical Efficiency Test (PET), six weeks after the date of confinement.  
If found fit, she is appointed to the post kept reserved for and allowed the benefit of 
seniority in accordance with the norms.

RATE OF DEATHS BY SUICIDE AMONGST YOUTH 
 
1970.  DR. KANIMOZHI NVN SOMU: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether it is a fact that rate of deaths by suicide is high amongst young 
adult, including females, between the age of 14 to 18 years and 18 to 24 
years and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) whether the Ministry has carried out a study to identify the prominent 
causes for such suicides, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c) the steps taken by the Ministry to address this issue; and 
 
(d) the steps taken by Government in collaboration with Ministry of Health 
and Family Welfare, for betterment of health of such youths? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
 
(a) & (b): National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) compiles and publishes 
data on suicides in its publication ‘Accidental Deaths & Suicides in India 
(ADSI)’.  The published reports are available till the year 2020. NCRB does 
not publish data about ‘Rate of suicides’ by female, youth, etc., separately. 
However, there are various causes for suicides such as family issues, 
extra-marital affairs, love affairs, marriage related issues, divorce, illness, 
poverty, indebtedness, property disputes, etc. 
206

-2- 
R.S.US.Q.NO. 1970 FOR 03.08.2022 
(c) & (d):  With a view to address the burden of mental disorders, the 
Government of India is supporting implementation of the District Mental 
Health Programme (DMHP) under the National Mental Health Programme 
(NMHP) in 704 districts of the country for which support is provided to 
States/UTs through the National Health Mission.  Facilities  made available 
under DMHP at the Community Health Centre(CHC) and Primary Health 
Centre(PHC) levels, 
inter-alia, include outpatient services, assessment, 
counselling/ psycho -social interventions, continuing care and support to 
persons with severe mental disorders, drugs, outreach services, 
ambulance services etc. In addition to above services there is a provision 
of 10 bedded in -patient facility at the District level. The objectives of 
DMHP are: 
(i) to provide suicide prevention services, work place stress 
management, life skills training and counselling in schools and 
colleges. 
(ii) to provide mental health services including prevention, promotion 
and long-term continuing care at different levels of district 
healthcare delivery system. 
(iii) to augment institutional capacity in terms of infrastructure, 
equipment and human resource for mental healthcare. 
207

-3- 
R.S.US.Q.NO. 1970 FOR 03.08.2022 
 
(iv) to promote community awareness and participation in the delivery of 
mental healthcare services. 
Under DMHP various Information, Education and Communication (IEC) 
activities such as awareness messages in local newspapers and radio, 
street plays, wall paintings etc. are taken by the States/ UTs. Further, 
funds are provided to each district supported under DMHP for targeted 
interventions which include following objectives: 
(i) To provide class teachers with a system of referral for students with 
psychological problems to the District Mental Health Team for inputs 
and treatment. 
(ii) To involve other stakeholders like parents, community leaders to 
enhance development of adolescents etc.

FUNCTIONING OF NIA 
 
1971.  SHRI G.V.L. NARASIMHA RAO: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the efforts made by Government to strengthen the National 
Investigation Agency (NIA) in recent years; 
 
(b) the number of cases being handled by NIA at present; 
 
(c) details of increase in the number of cases over the years, year-wise and 
the reasons therefor; 
 
(d) whether there is a need for better regulation and engagement of 
experts in NIA for speedy investigation of cases; and 
 
(e) if so, the details in this regard and Government's efforts and plans to 
bring about these changes? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
 
(a) to (e): The Central Government reviews administrative and legal 
requirements of National Investigation Agency (NIA) from time to time. 
Since 2019, the Government has taken several measures to enhance 
capacity of the NIA, which include as under: 
I. The NIA Act was amended in year 2019 to enlarge the mandate of the 
NIA by inclusion of offences related to human trafficking, 
manufacture & sale of prohibited arms, cyber -terrorism and offences 
under the Explosive Substances Act, 1908 and expand its 
jurisdictions beyond India. 
 
209

 
-2- 
R.S.US.Q.NO. 1971 FOR 03.08.2022 
II. Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 was amended in year 2019 
to empower DG (NIA) to seize/attach the properties related to 
proceeds of terrorism in cases being investigated by the NIA.  
III. In order to enhance capacity of NIA in terms of specialists, th e 
financial powers delegated to Director General of NIA for engaging 
consultants/ experts/ professionals have been enhanced.  
IV. 481 posts and 10 new branch offices at Chandigarh, Ranchi, Imphal, 
Chennai, Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Patna, Jaipur, Bhopal and 
Bhubaneswar have been sanctioned. 
Since its inception, the Central Government has entrusted 473 cases to 
the National Investigation Agency (NIA) for investigation.  The year-wise 
details are as under:-   
2009 08 
2010 11 
2011 16 
2012 16 
2013 27 
2014 14 
2015 21 
2016 34 
2017 36 
2018 59 
2019 62 
2020 59 
2021 61 
2022 (up to 29th July) 49 
Total 473 
 
The increase in registration of cases by the NIA over the years is mainly 
due to the enhanced capacity of NIA with sanction of new Branch offices 
and the augmented scope of NIA.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1974 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 03RD AUGUST, 2022/ SRAVANA 12, 1944 (SAKA) 
 
ASSAM FLOODS 
 
1974.  SHRI VIVEK K. TANKHA: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) how many people have lost lives and got displaced in the recent Assam 
floods; 
 
(b) whether any temporary shelters have been provided to displaced 
people if so, details thereof; 
 
(c) the amount of compensatory relief provided to the people affected; 
 
(d) the quantum of monetary loss suffered by the State and the common 
people in the recent floods; and 
 
(e) whether Government has got any plans to mitigate the frequent floods 
that affect various parts of the country especially Bihar and Assam, if so, 
details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
 
(a) to (d): The primary responsibility for disaster management rests with 
the State Governments concerned. The State Governments undertake 
relief measures in the wake of natural disasters from the State Disaster 
Response Fund (SDRF), already placed at their disposal, in accordance 
with the Government of India’s approved items and norms.  Additional 
financial assistance is provided from the National Disaster Response Fund  
222

-2- 
R.S.US.Q.NO. 1974 FOR 03.08.2022 
(NDRF), as per laid down procedure in case of disaster of ‘severe nature’, 
which includes an assessment based on the visit of an Inter-Ministerial 
Central Team (IMCT). 
During the south-west monsoon of 2022, floods and landslides reported to 
have caused extensive damages in various districts in the State of Assam.  
The State-wise information on losses caused due to natural calamities is 
not maintained centrally by this Ministry.  However, as per information 
furnished by the State Government of Assam, details of losses and relief 
camps are given as under:- 
(Provisional
) 
Human lives lost 
(As on 22.07.2022) 
Number of Relief Camps set-up by the State 
Government 
197  4075 – Relief Camps 
 5802 – Relief Distribution Centers  
 
Further, the Central Government, without waiting for the Memorandum 
from the State Government of Assam, has constituted an IMCT on 19 th May, 
2022, for on the spot assessment of damages.  IMCT has visited the State 
of Assam from 26 th to 29 th May, 2022 and second time from 30 th June to 3 rd 
July, 2022.  The Central Government has released both the installments of 
SDRF of the year 2022-23 totaling Rs. 648.80 crore, in advance, to help the 
State   Government  of  Assam  to  provide  relief 
  to  the  affected  people.   
223

-3- 
R.S.US.Q.NO. 1974 FOR 03.08.2022 
Distribution of the relief amount to the affected people in Assam is the 
responsibility of the State Government.   
(e): There are well established institutional mechanisms at the National, 
State & District levels in the country to develop appropriate preparedness 
and prompt response mechanisms for effective management of natural 
disasters including floods.  Central Government has established a robust 
early warning system and has significantly enhanced the accuracy of 
weather forecasts. Mock exercises and community awareness 
programmes are being regularly conducted to educate people about 
natural calamities including floods. 
Based on the recommendations of the 15 th Finance Commission, Central 
Government has allocated Rs. 13693.00 crore for National Disaster 
Mitigation Fund (NDMF) and Rs. 32030.60 crore for State Disaster 
Mitigation Fund (SDMF) for the period 2021-22 to 2025-26.  The State 
Governments can undertake mitigation activities for various disasters, 
including floods, as per the guidelines issued by the Ministry of Home 
Affairs for SDMF and NDMF on 14.01.2022 and 28.02.2022, respectively.  
Besides, the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) has issued 
Guidelines on ‘Management of Floods’  in 2008.  Presently, flood forecasts 
are issued by the Central Water  Commission (CWC) at 332 stations spread  
224

-4- 
R.S.US.Q.NO. 1974 FOR 03.08.2022 
across the country as per Standard Operating Procedure.  Annually, about 
8000 flood forecasts are issued by CWC during floods.   
The measures taken by the Central and the State Governments have 
significantly improved the disaster management practices, preparedness, 
prevention and response mechanisms resulting in significant reduction in 
casualties during natural calamities, including floods, in the country.  
Further, strengthening of the disaster management is a continuing and 
evolving process of the governance.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1975 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 03RD AUGUST, 2022/ SRAVANA 12, 1944 (SAKA) 
 
DELIMITATION OF MUNICIPAL WARDS IN DELHI 
 
1975.  SHRI SUSHIL KUMAR GUPTA: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Ministry has set up a three-member 
commission for carrying out a fresh delimitation of the municipal wards in 
Delhi; 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c) whether any number of wards has been declared so far; and 
 
(d) if not, how will this commission work without fixing the number of 
wards? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
 
(a) to (d ):  Sections 3, 3A and 5 of the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 
1957, confer the power of delimitation on the Central Government. In 
exercise of this power, the Central Government has constituted a three 
member committee to assist the Central Government in car rying out the 
delimitation of wards and other functions incidental or related thereto. 
Further, as per sub-section (6) of Section 3 of the said Act, the total 
number of wards shall not exceed two hundred and fifty.

State/Union Territory-wise and year-wise details of the number of

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1977 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 3RD  AUGUST, 2022/ SRAVANA 12, 1944 (SAKA) 
 
 SECURITY OF COURTS 
 
1977  SHRI ABIR RANJAN BISWAS: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether Government is aware of the incidence of escaping undertrial 
prisoners, firing and bomb blasts inside the court complex in Delhi, Punjab 
and many other parts of the country; 
 
(b) if so, whether there is a central guideline for handling of undertrial 
prisoners and security of courts; 
 
(c) if so, date of its last revision, details thereof; 
 
(d) whether Government is considering deploying CISF for the security of 
High Courts and training of the State police at the central level for the 
security of district courts; and 
 
(e) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
(a) to (c): As per entry 4 of List II of the Seventh Schedule to the 
Constitution of India 'Prisons'/'persons detained therein' is a “State 
List” subject. Administration and management of prisons and 
prisoners is the responsibility of respective State Governments. 
However, the Ministry of  Home  Affairs  (MHA)  provides  guidance  to  
 
230

-2- 
R.S.USQ.NO.1977 FOR 03.08.2022 
 
States and Union Territories (UTs) on varied aspects of prison 
administration. A Model Prison Manual, 2016 has been prepared by 
MHA and circulated to all States and UTs.  
‘Police’ and ‘Public Order’ are State subjects and, therefore, providing 
security to the courts is the responsibility of the State Governments 
concerned.  However, MHA has also issued guidelines for the security 
of High Courts and District/ Subordinate Courts in the country on 
04.07.2007 addressed to all State Government/ UT Administrations 
and Police heads. These guidelines provide a comprehensive 
mechanism for security system specialized for the protection of 
judicial bodies and its properties.  The guidelines also stipulate that 
there should be Specialized Unit/ Branch within the State/ UT police 
to look after the security of Judges/ Courts. The guidelines were 
reiterated on 24.03.2020. 
(d) and (e) : There is no  proposal under consideration for the 
deployment of the CISF for the security of High Courts.  However, in 
pursuance of the orders of Hon’ble High Court of Madras in suo   
motu WP No. 29197 of 2015, CISF personnel are deployed on  IS  duty  
pattern on cost-re-imbursement basis at Madras High Court and the 
Madurai Bench of Madras High Court.

MANAGEMENT OF VILLAGE HAATS

(a)  whether Government has district-wise data relating to number and location of Village 
Haats or Weekly Markets in the country; 
(b)  whether Government intends to undertake a project to create platforms and shades for 
Village Haats which are generally organised in open spaces; 
(c)  whether a Committee can be set up to suggest to sale purchase of village products 
from Haats to cut middleman interest; and 
(d)  whether an audit of Gram Panchayats has been done by District Administration 
regarding Panchayat’s designated responsibility to manage Village Haats? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SADHVI N
IRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a)  No, Sir  
  
(b)  The development and upgradation of physical infrastructure including platforms and 
shades of rural haats is being undertaken through Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment 
Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) as per demand and following due processes of the 
Mahatma 
Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act.The State-wise status of village haat works 
under MGNREGS (as uploaded by the State/UTs in MIS) as on 30th July 2022 is given at 
Annexure-I 
  
Under the scheme of ‘Mechanism for Marketing of Minor Forest Produce (MFP) through 
Minimum Support Price (MSP) and Development of Value Chain for MFP’ (now merged under 
Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission), the Ministry of Tribal Affairs provides funds for 
creation of Infrastructure facilities for development of MFP value chain including modernization 
of Haat Bazaars. The Ministry of Tribal Affairs has released an amount of Rs. 89.16 crores to 18 
States under the scheme from 2013-14 to 2020-21 for creation of Infrastructure facilities 
including modernization of Haat Bazaars. The State-wise number of Haat Bazaars sanctioned to 
be modernized under the scheme from the fund mentioned above 
 is given at Annexure-II.  
  
(c)  At present, there is no proposal for  setting up the Committee to suggest to sale purchase 
of village products from Haats. 
  
(d)  No, Sir.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1979 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 3RD  AUGUST, 2022/ SRAVANA 12, 1944 (SAKA) 
 
 ANTI-LYNCHING LAW 
 
1979  SHRI SANJAY SINGH: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Ministry has set up a committee to bring anti-lynching law; 
 
(b) if so, details thereof; and 
 
(c) if not, then, whether Government plans to bring such a law to curb the 
menace of mob justice in the country? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
(a) to (c): It is the intention of the Government to comprehensively review 
the existing Criminal Laws and make them relevant to the contemporary 
law and order situation as well as to provide speedy justice to the 
vulnerable sections of the society and create a legal structure which is 
citizen-centric. The Department–related Parliamentary Standing 
Committee on Home Affairs, in its 146th Report dated 23.06.2010, had 
recommended that there is a need for a comprehensive review of the 
Criminal  Justice   System   of   the   country.   Earlier   the   Parliamentary  
Standing  Committee  in  its  111th  and  128th  Reports  had   also  stressed  
 
235

-2- 
R.S.USQ.NO.1979 FOR 03.08.2022 
upon  the need to reform and rationalize the criminal law of the country  by  
introducing a comprehensive legislation in Parliament rather than bringing 
about piecemeal amendments in respective Acts. Government of India is 
committed to make comprehensive amendments to criminal laws in 
consultation with all the stakeholders.

NCRB DATA ON MOB LYNCHINGS

(e) if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
(a) & (b): In the year 2017, National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) 
collected data from States on cases of mob lynchings and  hate crimes, 
but it was observed that the data was unreliable. 
(c) to (e): It is the intention of the Government to comprehensively review 
the existing Criminal Laws and make them relevant to the contemporary 
law  and  order  situation   as  well  as  to  provide  speedy   justice  to   the 
237

-2- 
R.S.USQ.NO.1980 FOR 03.08.2022 
vulnerable sections of the society and create a legal structure which is 
citizen-centric. The Department–related Parliamentary Standing 
Committee on Home Affairs, in its 146th Report dated 23.06.2010, had 
recommended that there is a need for a comprehensive review of the 
Criminal Justice System of the country. Earlier the Parliamentary Standing 
Committee in its 111th and 128th Reports had also stressed upon the need 
to reform and rationalize the criminal law of the country by introducing a 
comprehensive legislation in Parliament rather than bringing about piece-

to make comprehensive amendments to criminal laws in consultation with

HAMARI DHAROHAR SCHEME 
  
1988 DR. SANTANU SEN: 
Will the Minister of MINORITY AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the allocation of budget and funds utilization under Hamari Dharohar scheme for 
preservation of minorities heritage buildings since 2017; 
(b) the number of heritage buildings under Hamari Dharohar scheme, State-wise, year-wise 
since inception of scheme; 
(c) whether it is a fact that the number of attempts for destroying minority heritage buildings 
has increased in recent years, the details of all such incidents in last five years; and  
(d) the steps taken to ensure that such incidents are avoided? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF MINORITY AFFAIRS 
(SHRIMATI SMRITI ZUBIN IRANI) 
  
(a) & (b) "Hamari Dharohar” scheme has been formulated to preserve rich heritage of minority 
communities of India. The scheme provides for curating rich heritage of minorities under overall 
concept of Indian Culture which includes curating exhibitions, preservation of literature/ 
documents etc. Preservation of minority heritage buildings has not been undertaken so far under 
the Hamari Dharohar Scheme. The budget and funds utilization under Hamari Dharohar Scheme 
during previous financial years since 2016-17 are as below (Figures in Rs. Crore):- 
 
Year RE Expenditure
 
  
2016-17 8.00 6.60 
2017-18 12.00 0.64 
2018-19 6.00 1.64 
2019-20 3.00 0.70 
2020-21 5.20 4.55 
2021-22 2.00 1.66 
259

 
 
 
(c) & (d)  “Public Order” is a State subject as per the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of 
India. The responsibility of maintaining law and order, registration and prosecution of crimes 
against life and property of all citizens including minorities, rests with the respective State 
Governments. Ministry has not received report of damage to minority heritage buildings from 
states.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1989 
ANSWERED ON 03.08.2022 
  
SECURITY AND PROTECTION OF MINORITY COMMUNITIES 
  
1989.  SHRI ABDUL WAHAB: 
  
Will the Minister of MINORITY AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Minority Commission has received complaints from the representatives or 
persons from minority community in regard to communal attack they are being 
exposed to; 
(b) if so, the complaints that the commission has received in the last five years, the  
yearwise details thereof; 
(c) what action has been taken up by Government to resolve the complaints  received; 
(d) whether the commission has taken cognizance of the increasing communal attack 
against Muslim community in different parts of the country; and 
(e) if so, what action has been taken by the commission to ensure security of  minority 
communities?  
  
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF MINORITY AFFAIRS 
(SHRIMATI SMRITI ZUBIN IRANI)  
 (a)  to (e)  “Public Order” and “Police” are State subjects as per the Seventh Schedule 
of the Constitution of India. The responsibility of maintaining law and order, 
registration and prosecution of crimes against all citizens including minorities, rests 
with the respective State Governments. Government of India monitors the internal 
security and law and order situation in the country and issues appropriate advisories 
to States from time to time to maintain peace, public tranquility and communal 
harmony. Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) are deployed to aid and assist State 
Governments, on their request, to maintain law and order and public tranquility. 
Government of India has issued communal Harmony Guidelines, which, inter-alia 
lay down standard operating procedure to deal with situations arising out of 
communal violence. These guidelines are aimed to maintain due vigilance, careful 
planning and preparatory measures to prevent and pre-empt communal violence. 
  
261

Further, the details of the complaints with the National Commission for Minorities 
(NCM), in the last five years is annexed. 
  
Whenever NCM receives any complaint in the matter, reports are called from the 
concerned Authorities. In some cases, when the report is not satisfactory, NCM also 
conducts hearings to resolve the issue. Further, in cases of media reports, NCM takes 
suo moto cognizance and calls for report.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1990 
ANSWERED ON 03/08/2022  
 
EMPOWERING PANCHAYATS  
 
 1990# DR. SUMER SINGH SOLANKI:  
 
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Government is implementing any scheme to provide adequate infrastructure to 
the Panchayats in the country especially in the State of Madhya Pradesh; 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(c) the details of the steps taken to encourage the States to devolve more powers to the 
Panchayats? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI KAPIL MORESHWAR PATIL) 
 
(a) to (c) Panchayat being a State subject, devolution of power and providing infrastructural 
facilities such as Gram Panchayat Bhawans, computers and peripherals etc are primarily the 
responsibility of the States. However, Mi nistry of Panchayati Raj supplements the efforts of 
the States including Madhya Pradesh, through its revamped scheme of Rashtriya Gram Swaraj 
Abhiyan (RGSA) approved on 13.04.2022 for implementation from 01.04.2022 to 31.03.2026 
provides financial support for infrastructure on a limited scale with special focu s on North 
Eastern States.  
 
Further, Article 243G allows discretion to the States in the matter of devolution of 
powers (funds, functions and functionaries) to Panchayats. The States vary in the extent to 
which they have devolved powers to the Panchayats to plan, implement and monitor schemes 
for economic development and social justice. Ministry of Panchayati Raj has continuously been 
advocating and persuading through advisories, letters, meetings, workshop, conferences etc. 
with the State Governments to devolve powers to the Panchayats.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1991

DIGITISING PANCHAYAT OFFICES 
 
1991.  SHRI RAJMANI PATEL: 
 
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to State: 
 
(a) the State -wise data on the number and percentage of Panchayat offices that have 
computer and internet connection; 
(b) the steps taken by Government to digitise Panchayat institutions and offices; 
(c) the annual budget allocation and final expenditure on e-Panchayat mission mode project 
in the last five years; and 
(d) the outcome status of the e-Panchayat mission mode project? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI KAPIL MORESHWAR PATIL) 
 
(a) Panchayat being State subject, providing computers for Panchayats is primarily the 
responsibility of States/ Union Territories (UTs). However, Ministry, under the sche me of 
Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA)supplemented the efforts of all States by providing 
computers for Panchayats as proposed by States/UTs in their Annual Action Plan and approved 
by Central Empowered Committee, on a limited scale. For attaining the vision of Digital India, 
BharatNet project is being implemented by Department of Telecommunications in a phased 
manner to create network to connect all the Gram Panchayats by broadband in the country. The 
scope of BharatNet on 30.06.2021 has been extended up to all inhabited villages beyond GPs 
in the country. The State/UT -wise details of Gram panchayats having computers and internet 
connection is given at Annexure-I. 
(b) Under Digital India Programme, Ministry is implementing e -Panchayat Mission Mode 
Project (MMP) with the aim to transform the functioning of Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs), 
making them more transparent, accountable, and effective. The Ministry launched 
eGramSwaraj, a work-based Accounting Application for Panchayati Raj Institutions under the 
e-Panchayat MMP on 24th April 2020. This application encompasses all aspects of Panchayat 
265

functioning viz. planning, budgeting, accounting, monitoring, asset management etc, on a 
single digital platform including online payments. 
(c) Under e -Panchayat Mission Mode Project funds are being provided to National 
Informatics Center Services Inc. (NICSI) for central level support for maintenance of e -
Panchayat applications. The year wise annual expenditure on E -Panchayat Mission Mode 
Project is given at Annexure-II. 
(d) So far, 2.53 lakh GPs have prepared and uploaded their Gram Panchayat Development 
Plans (GPDPs)for 2022-23 on E-GramSwaraj. Under 14th Finance Commission, 1.44 lakh GPs 
and 91,607 GPs have carried out online transactions during 2020-21 and 2021-22 respectively. 
Similarly, 1.93 lakh GPs have carried online transactions under 15 thFinance Commission 
during 2021-22. All States are making efforts to implement e-Panchayat MMP, based on their 
available resources and here is substantial improvement in adoption of digital applications by 
the States in PRIs functioning.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO -1992 
ANSWERED ON –03/08/2022 
 
DATA OF TREES CUT ALONG ROADS AND HIGHWAYS 
 
1992.  SHRI NARESH BANSAL: 
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether large number of trees along the existing r oads and highways had to be cut during 
the process of widening of roads, specially in Uttarakhand, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the number of trees cut for the construction of D elhi -Dehradun express highway from 
Ganeshpur to Dehradun in Rajaji National Park, Mohand jungle; 
(c) action taken by NHAI on replantation along this highway, details of re -plantation projects 
of tress on Rajaji National Park highway; and 
(d) the details of plantation projects along the highways completed by March, 2021? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a)  Development of National Highways (NHs) involves clearing Right of Way (RoW) 
acquired by the Ministry. It is always ensured that the bare minimum tree felling is carried out 
for widening of existing NHs.  
(b) A total 7,747 trees and 3,258 saplings have been cut down in Shivalik  forest division 
for Delhi-Dehradun expressway project from Ganeshpur to Dehradun. None of these trees were 
within the boundary of Rajaji National Park. 
(c) About 1.76 lakh trees are to be planted as per Compensatory Afforestation scheme 
prepared by Uttar Pradesh & Uttarakhand Forest Departments.  An amount of Rs. 844.13 Lakhs 
have been deposited by National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) to Uttar Pradesh & 
Uttarakhand Forest Departments towards Compensatory Afforestation and Net Present Value. 
Apart from above, NHAI has trans-located 155 trees.  
(d) 55.10 lakh plants have been planted in 94 projects, completed by March 2021.

1995. SHRI AJIT KUMAR BHUYAN:

 Assam into six lanes; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) how many kilometers of NH in Assam is yet to be completed into four lanes till now; and 
(d) what amount had been expended for four lanes NH in Assam so far, the details thereof year -
 wise for the last five years?

to Jorabat junction (Km. 171.050) on NH 37 including Flyover / Trumpet Interchange at Jorabat 
Junction (8.50 Km) is in DPR stage. 
  
(c) At present, the balance length of NH under upgradation/development to 4 lane configuration is 
350 km.

GIS MAPPING OF HIGHWAYS 
 
1996 # SHRI NARHARI AMIN: 
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is proposed to make GIS mapping by integrating the country's highway network; 
(b) if so, the manner in which it would be useful for the transport service of the country; 
(c) whether this mapping would also speed up the construction work of the h ighways, if so, the 
details thereof; and 
(d) the total percentage of mapping work that has been completed in Gujarat, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) to (c) The Ministry has taken initiatives for GIS mapping of the National Highways 
network on the PM Gati Shakti NMP portal. Total length of NHs in the Country is about 
1,41,720 km. So far, NHs length of about 1,41,190 km has been mapped on the PM Gati Shakti 
NMP Portal.   This en visages coordinated and integrated planning, project preparations and 
implementation, optimization of logistics arrangements and efficient transportation systems.  
(d) Entire 7,885 km length of NHs network in the State of Gujarat has been mapped on PM 
Gati Shakti NMP Portal; out of these, alignments of about 4,503 km length of NHs have been 
validated so far.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-1997 
ANSWERED ON-03/08/2022 
MANDATORY SAFETY STANDARDS FOR LMV 
 
1997.   SHRI S. SELVAGANABATHY: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state :- 
(a)  whether Government has conducted any study to ascertain the number of deaths in road 
accidents involving Light Motor Vehicles (LMVs) not meeting prescribed safety standards; 
(b)  if so, the details and outcome thereof; 
(c)  whether Government has introduced a mandatory recall policy for vehicles which does not 
meet prescribed safety standards; and 
(d)  if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) & (b) As per “Road Accidents in India 2020” published by Ministry of Road Transport & 
Highways, the percentage share of persons killed in road accidents in terms of Road-user category 
of Cars, Taxis, Vans & LMVs was 16.6%, 15.8% & 13.7 % in 2018, 2019 and 2020 re spectively. 
The Central Government has taken various measures including mandatory fitment of one air bag 
with effect from 0 1.07.2019, two air bags with effect from 31.12.2021, off -set frontal crash test 
norms with effect from 01. 10.2019 among other safety provisions on M1 Category vehicles with 
Gross Vehicle Weight up to 2.5 tonnes.  
(c) & (d) Section 110A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is related to recall of motor vehicles. 
It empowers the Central Government to direct a manufacturer to recall motor vehicles of a particular 
type or its variants, if- 
  
(a)  a defect in that particular type of motor vehicle may cause harm to the environment or 
to the driver or occupants of such motor vehicle or other road users; and 
(b)  a defect in that particular type of motor vehicle has been reported to the Central 
Government by— 
(i)  such percentage of owners, as the Central Government may, by notification in the 
Official Gazette, specify; or 
(ii)  a testing agency; or 
(iii)  any other source. 
  
Also, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways vide G.S.R. 173(E) dated 11th March, 2021 
has inserted a new rule 127C in Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 which prescribes the procedure 
for recall of defective motor vehicles and recall notice.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT & HIGHWAYS 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 2000 
ANSWERED ON- 03/08/ 2022 
 
FUNDS SANCTIONED FOR REPAIR AND MAINTENANCE OF NATIONAL 
HIGHWAYS IN MAHARASHTRA 
 
2000. DR. FAUZIA KHAN: 
 
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state:    
 
(a)  the funds sanctioned for the repair and maintenance of National Highways in 
Maharashtra State during the last five years till date, year-wise; 
 
(b)  whether Government is aware that lack of repairs and maintenance of National 
Highways has rendered most of the roads dilapidated which often cause accidents and 
creates difficulty in movement of traffic; 
 
(c)  whether any action has been taken against contractors and officers who do not follow 
the norms specified for qualitative construction of roads; and 
 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) All National Highway (NH) Projects are bid out for construction and maintenance for a fixed 
period. Hence maintenance of NH is regularly provided for. 
  
(b) NHs are maintained in traffic worthy condition and Maintenance/Repair works are taken up as 
required. 
  
(c) &(d) As per the provisions of contract/concession agreement, the contractor has to ensure the 
construction, material and quality of workmanship is in accordance with the Ministry’s Manual, 
IRC codes and good industry practice. In case of any deviation, Authority’s Engineer issues Non-
Compliance Report (NCR) to the  contractor, which is to be rectified by the Contractor during 
construction period as well as operation & maintenance period.
